:::{#def-inner-product-space}
#### Inner product space

An **inner product space** is a pair $(\reals^p, \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot})$
of the space $\reals^p$ (@def-real-coordinate-space)
and an inner product $\iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}$ on it (@def-inner-product).
We say that $\reals^p$ is **equipped with** that inner product:
the inner product is part of the data of the space,
so the same set of vectors with a different inner product is a different inner product space.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-inner-product-space}
#### Real coordinate space as an inner product space

The Euclidean space $\reals^p$ equipped with the standard dot product (@def-dot-product),
that is, the pair $(\reals^p, \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot})$ with $\iprod{\vx}{\vy} = \vx \cdot \vy$,
is an inner product space, because the dot product satisfies the four inner product axioms (@exm-dot-product-inner-product).
For $p = 2$, any vector $\vx = (x_1, x_2) \in \reals^2$ has squared norm $\iprod{\vx}{\vx} = x_1^2 + x_2^2 \ge 0$,
which is zero if and only if

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_1 &= x_2 \\
&= 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Equipping the same vector space $\reals^p$ with different inner products
yields different inner product spaces with different geometric notions of angle and distance on the same set of vectors.

:::
